clue.text: Cut short drum'n'bass in club

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, so the tail of the drum comes off

parts.note: drum with its last letter cut
B is the musical abbreviation for bass

explanation.surface: A club night's set of drum'n'bass gets cut off early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drum'n'bass' reads as the music genre, but it splits into drum, 'n' (and) and bass; 'club' is the verb at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To drub someone is to beat them thoroughly, just as to club them is to strike with a heavy stick.

clue.text: Easy target saving crooked donor

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: saving in the sense of except, which is also what bar means
the letters of donor rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest benefactor is an easy mark for fraud investigators who want to keep the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like rescuing or putting money aside, but here it means 'except', the preposition BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as big as a barn door is proverbially impossible to miss, hence an easy target.

clue.text: Singer James Blunt reportedly goes ahead to make open sandwich

indicators.note: going ahead places this piece in front of the singer's name
what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: blunt means brusque, and brusque spoken sounds like the opening of the Italian word
Etta James, the American soul and blues singer

explanation.surface: The singer James Blunt is said to be pressing on with making himself a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'James Blunt' is a real singer, but the clue splits him: 'Singer James' is Etta James, and 'Blunt' is the brusque word that sounds like the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruschetta is Italian toasted bread topped with tomato and oil, served without a lid, so it counts as an open sandwich.

clue.text: Some funding is never returned; this could be a red flag

definitions.text: this could be a red flag

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the run is read right to left
only some of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters straddling fundiNG IS NEver

explanation.surface: A warning that funding never comes back is a red flag for investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red flag' looks like a warning sign, but the Red Ensign is the literal red flag flown by British merchant ships.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a naval flag, and the Red Ensign is one example, so a red flag could be one.

clue.text: Feud led bishop to stir disorder

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A quarrel led a churchman to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' reads as a noun, the trouble stirred up, but it is the verb meaning to throw into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To befuddle someone is to muddle their thinking, which is to disorder it.

clue.text: Broadcast follows Labour leader in retreat

indicators.note: one piece following the other sets the order: the party letter comes first
a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the party name is kept

parts.note: first letter of Labour
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A broadcast follows the Labour Party leader while they are on an away-day retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a political away-day, but it is the noun for a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den, a place to retreat to and hide.

clue.text: Head of Football League stopping team getting debilitating illness

indicators.note: these letters stop up the team's name by sitting in its middle like a plug

parts.note: Man U, the common short name of Manchester United football club

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of Football
L is the abbreviation for League

explanation.surface: A Football League boss stops a team from playing because the players are ill.
explanation.walkthrough: MANU, Manchester United, is split around F and L. Man flu is a joking term for a cold that a man claims is crippling, hence the tongue-in-cheek 'debilitating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Man flu mocks the idea that a mild cold leaves men completely incapacitated, so 'debilitating illness' is said with irony.

clue.text: Observed setting for audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: a scene is the setting of a story or play

explanation.surface: Someone was watched while setting up for an audition at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests a theatre tryout, which fits 'setting', but it is used in its literal sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen is the past participle of see, so it means observed or watched.

clue.text: Reform bring up diversity

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
a range is a varied spread of things

explanation.surface: A call for reform to promote diversity in the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring up' reads as raising a topic, but here it is raising a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange something is to put it into a new order, which is to reform its structure.

clue.text: Accepted women are enlightened

parts.note: A is a recognised abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is now accepted that women are enlightened.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware of something is to be informed about it, which is one sense of being enlightened.

clue.text: Extra responsibility follows job's termination

indicators.note: following sets the order: the job's last letter comes first and the other piece after it
a word's termination is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of job
an onus is a duty or burden of responsibility

explanation.surface: Taking on more responsibility after being sacked earns an extra payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'termination' reads as being fired from a job, but it only points at the job's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an additional payment or benefit on top of what is expected.

clue.text: Police fire on pub which produces drug

indicators.note: to police is to regulate and sort out, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Police open fire on a pub selling drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' looks like the noun firing on the pub, but it is a verb meaning to control, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common anti-inflammatory painkiller, an example of a drug.

clue.text: Hormone transforms common bird

indicators.note: a transformation changes the shape of something, so the letters are recast

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hormone makes an ordinary bird change, as in a nature documentary.
explanation.definitionFit: The moorhen is a black waterbird found on ponds and rivers across Britain, so it is a familiar, common species.

clue.text: Second place for twisting symbolic design

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time like a second

indicators.note: twisting turns something round, so the word for place is read backwards

parts.note: to fit a part is to place it in position

explanation.surface: A second spot is chosen for a twisting pattern with symbolic meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal before 'place', as in runner-up, but it is a moment of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring decorative or thematic element, a design carrying meaning.

clue.text: Dry and skiddy, oddly? Turned round, creating inconvenience

indicators.note: turning everything round means the joined pieces are read from back to front

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

parts.note: the odd letters of skiddy

explanation.surface: A car on a dry but slippery road spins round, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUT is the wine term for dry champagne; 'Dry and skiddy' sounds contradictory for a road surface, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to interrupt or bother them, which is to inconvenience them.

clue.text: Unmarried woman plays with hair

parts.note: a DJ spins records, i.e. plays them
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A single woman fiddles with her hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinster is the old word for an unmarried woman; the -stress spelling is a playful variant built for this clue's wordplay.

clue.text: Drink a lot, being reckless

indicators.note: reckless behaviour is wild and disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning against heavy drinking because it is reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: To binge is to overindulge, especially to consume large amounts of alcohol in one session.

clue.text: Left-winger receives a card

indicators.note: what receives something takes it inside, so the letter goes in the middle

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a far-left activist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician gets a card, perhaps a membership card or a red card.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of the cards in a fortune-telling pack, so it is a kind of card.

clue.text: Bladed tool in Mike's shed

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the letter belonging to the radio name is dropped

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: A garden tool kept in Mike's shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the garden building where a tool lives; it is the verb, so HOME sheds Mike's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a long-handled garden tool with a flat blade used for weeding.

clue.text: Thus gets naked with duke in county town

indicators.note: getting naked means stripping off the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: thus means therefore, here without its outer letters
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke is caught naked in a provincial town, so the scandal goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is the county town of Herefordshire, in the west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford is the administrative centre of Herefordshire, which is what a county town is.

clue.text: Japan losing first point that would win match

indicators.note: losing the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Nippon is the Japanese name for Japan

explanation.surface: Japan's team loses the first point in a match it could have won.
explanation.walkthrough: An ippon is a full point in judo, scored by a clean throw or hold, which ends the bout at once.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo an ippon is the decisive full-point score that wins the contest outright.

clue.text: Almost immaculate American city

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pristine, spotless, without its final letter
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American city is nearly spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American city' looks like a single phrase pointing to a US city, but American only gives a letter and the city is in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristina is the capital of Kosovo, a city in the Balkans.

clue.text: France not just an exciting place for kids

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
not just means unjust, i.e. unfair

explanation.surface: France is not merely a fun destination for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just' reads as 'not only', but 'just' is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair, with its rides and stalls, is a place of thrills that children love.

clue.text: Annoy Germans in river

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it

parts.note: the Nile, the African river
G is the abbreviation for German, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Germans paddling in a river irritate the locals.
explanation.definitionFit: To niggle is to irritate in a small, persistent way, a mild form of annoyance.

clue.text: Say I test solved Enigmatic Variations, primarily after recalling hint

indicators.note: recalling calls things back, so the gathered letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as when you say something
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives only its first letter

parts.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A solver boasts of test-solving an Enigmatic Variations puzzle, needing only a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigmatic Variations is a Sunday Telegraph thematic puzzle series; here it just supplies two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a small trace of something, which is a hint of it.

clue.text: Degenerate briefly provided end to discriminatory abuse

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: vile, morally degenerate, without its last letter
if, as in 'provided that'

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: last letter of discriminatory

explanation.surface: A degenerate briefly offered an end to discriminatory abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' looks like a noun, a person, but it is the adjective meaning vile.
explanation.definitionFit: To vilify is to speak abusively about someone, to abuse them verbally.

clue.text: Contrite, urge left and right to adapt

indicators.note: adapting changes something to suit, so these letters are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A repentant politician urges both left and right wings to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like an abbreviation alongside 'right', but it stays whole as fodder; only right shrinks to R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone regretful feels sorrow for what they did, which is being contrite.

clue.text: Remains bottom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a remnant, what is left
second meaning: the buttocks or hindquarters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains bottom' reads as something staying at the foot of a table; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is both a small leftover remnant of a larger body and an animal's hind part.

clue.text: Queen Street, at an earlier time

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina
St is the abbreviation for Street

explanation.surface: A street named after a queen, as it used to be called.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic word for formerly, the root of erstwhile.

clue.text: Pitiable soul told gag

indicators.note: something told is spoken out, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: a wretch is an unfortunate, pitiable person

explanation.surface: A miserable person is told a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a joke being told, but it is the verb for nearly vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if vomiting, which is what to gag means.

clue.text: Whisker regularly plucked for tramp

indicators.note: letters plucked at a regular interval are removed, here every third one starting with the first

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp's whisker is tidied up with tweezers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' reads as a vagrant with whiskers, but it is the verb for a long trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To hike is to walk a long distance on foot, which is what to tramp means.

clue.text: Little cycling seen in shopping centres

indicators.note: cycling moves round in a loop, so the first letter goes round to the back

parts.note: small means little

explanation.surface: Not much cycling goes on inside shopping centres.
explanation.definitionFit: Malls are large enclosed complexes of shops, the American word for shopping centres.

clue.text: Fire nukes at sea? I say no

definitions.note: a statement standing for the person who makes it

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked to launch nuclear missiles from a submarine, someone refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the refusenik's story; the definition is the refusal itself, spoken in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusenik is someone who refuses to comply, so the motto of such a person would be 'I say no'.
